collection_card.setting: A family shares one vehicle during commutes, long trips, and seasonal travel.
collection_card.author_instruction: Write what each person would naturally say inside the car. Do not expose Tool names, memory labels, or slot notation.
collection_card.assistant_role: A silent memory system observes the human conversation. The vehicle assistant is queried only in the Quiz items.

speakers.style: concise and practical; explains a preference after trying a setting

speakers.role: frequent front passenger and occasional driver
speakers.style: conversational; compares the current setting with earlier trips
informal and direct; notices glare while reading

sessions.context: Cold weekday morning. Maya is driving Daniel to work on an unfamiliar route.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: The windshield cleared fast, but it is still properly cold in here.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For these cold morning commutes, twenty degrees on my side feels comfortable. Please remember that as my usual setting.

update.condition: for Maya's cold morning commute when she is driving
update.reason: Maya explicitly commits to a durable driver-zone temperature for cold morning commutes.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: That would be too cool for me, but it is your side of the cabin.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I do not know this route well. On unfamiliar routes I want detailed voice guidance, and I would like that kept as my default.

update.condition: when Maya is driving an unfamiliar route
update.reason: Maya explicitly defines a persistent navigation voice preference for unfamiliar routes.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Fair. Missing one of these exits would add another twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Music at volume twenty-four is enough for my morning drives without covering the directions. Remember that one for me too.

update.reason: Maya states and asks to retain a durable morning-drive music volume.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: That balance works; I can hear both without either one shouting at us.

sessions.context: Evening family drive. Maya drives, Daniel is in the front passenger seat, and Zoe reads in the rear-left seat.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: This is much better than the freezing cabin we had at the start of the last long trip.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: When I am in the front passenger seat on a long trip, twenty-three degrees is comfortable. Please keep that as my setting.

update.condition: when Daniel is the front passenger on a long trip
update.reason: Daniel explicitly commits to a durable front-passenger temperature for long trips.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Good, keeping the two front zones separate should stop us negotiating every time.

turns.speaker: zoe
turns.text: Can someone bring up my reading light? The print in this book is tiny.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Try it at four and tell us whether it reflects in the side glass.

turns.speaker: zoe
turns.text: Four is clear enough right now. Save brightness four for my rear-left reading light whenever I read after dark.

update.condition: when Zoe reads in the rear-left seat after dark
update.reason: Zoe confirms brightness 4 and asks to save it for a recurring reading context.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I would also like warm orange ambient lighting whenever I drive at night. That is easier on my eyes, so remember orange for me.

update.condition: when Maya is driving at night
update.reason: Maya explicitly asks to retain orange ambient lighting for night driving.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Orange is calmer than that bright blue theme we tried at the dealership.

sessions.context: Another cold commute on an unfamiliar route. The family revises three earlier preferences after repeated use.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The navigation talked through every minor bend again yesterday. It was more distracting than helpful.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Change my unfamiliar-route guidance from detailed to simple from now on. I still want prompts, just fewer of them.

update.condition: when Maya is driving an unfamiliar route
update.reason: Maya explicitly replaces detailed guidance with simple guidance for the same recurring context.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Simple should still warn you before the complicated junction near the bridge.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Twenty degrees on my side has also felt too cool on the last few early starts.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Replace my cold-morning driver setting with twenty-two degrees instead of twenty. Use twenty-two going forward.

update.condition: for Maya's cold morning commute when she is driving
update.reason: Maya explicitly supersedes her old driver-zone temperature for the same condition.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: I have the opposite problem. Twenty-three in the passenger seat gets stuffy after an hour.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Change my front-passenger setting on long trips to twenty-one instead of twenty-three. Keep twenty-one as the new one.

update.condition: when Daniel is the front passenger on a long trip
update.reason: Daniel explicitly replaces his previous long-trip passenger temperature.

turns.speaker: zoe
turns.text: Please leave my side alone; the back feels fine and I am not even reading this morning.

sessions.context: Summer evening after Maya's gym session. Zoe tries her stored reading light again after sunset.

turns.speaker: zoe
turns.text: The page is easy to read, but level four is reflecting off the window now that it is fully dark.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Try two. We can change it permanently if that is still bright enough.

turns.speaker: zoe
turns.text: Two works. For reading after dark, change my rear-left lamp setting to brightness two instead of four.

update.condition: when Zoe reads in the rear-left seat after dark
update.reason: Zoe confirms a lower brightness and explicitly replaces the old value for the same context.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I am still overheated from the gym, even with the cabin cooling down.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: The seat ventilation will probably help more than lowering everybody's temperature.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Good idea. After summer gym trips when I am driving, remember driver-seat ventilation at speed two for me.

update.condition: after Maya's summer gym trips when she is driving
update.reason: Maya asks to remember a recurring driver-seat ventilation setting.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: That lets Zoe and me keep our zones where they are.

sessions.context: Cold weekend departure. Daniel is in the front passenger seat and the family discusses their lock-up routine.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: The seat is colder than the cabin this morning.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: For cold weekend drives when I am up front, remember passenger-seat heating at level one for me.

update.condition: for Daniel's cold weekend drives in the front passenger seat
update.reason: Daniel explicitly asks to retain a passenger-seat heating level for recurring cold weekend trips.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Level one makes sense if you are keeping your coat on.

turns.speaker: zoe
turns.text: Last week my window stayed cracked after we parked. I did not notice until we were inside.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For this shared car, let us have every window close automatically whenever we lock it. Keep that as the car-wide rule.

update.condition: whenever the shared vehicle is locked
update.reason: Maya establishes an explicit persistent rule for all windows in the shared vehicle.

turns.speaker: zoe
turns.text: Good. Then nobody has to walk back out just to check all four.

quizzes.query: Maya is starting another cold morning commute on an unfamiliar route. Apply the comfort and guidance settings she had asked us to remember.
Zoe has settled into the rear-left seat with her book after sunset. Put her reading light at the setting she just chose.
Maya is driving a cold morning commute on an unfamiliar route, with Daniel in the front passenger seat for a long trip. Use their latest remembered settings.
Maya is setting off on a cold morning commute along an unfamiliar route. Restore her current driving setup, including the music level she uses in the morning.
Daniel is taking the front passenger seat for a long drive. Set his side to the temperature he most recently settled on.
It is dark and Zoe is reading in her usual rear seat. Adjust her lamp to the corrected setting that avoids the window reflection.
Maya is driving after sunset. Use the ambient-light color she finds easier on her eyes.
Maya has just left the gym on a hot summer evening and is driving home. Apply the seat setting she asked to retain for this situation.
Daniel is sitting up front for a cold weekend drive. Warm his seat using his remembered preference.
Apply the shared family's window rule for the next time the vehicle is locked.
